description:

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the MCP query `work.get_context` (tool `work_get_context`) gains a per-item form. Nothing else of the parent (refusal details, wrapper reclaim, mission text) belongs here.

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.ts:156-159 `answerWorkContext` returns `bytesOf(config.affordances.readSurface())` - the WHOLE affordance surface regardless of payload; the file is 366 lines (hard cap 400): if the per-item branch pushes it past 400, extract the work-context handler into `mcp-work-context-query.ts` (+ `.js` bridge) rather than trimming elsewhere.
- Each `ChainStep` already carries `claim` and `claimAggregateVersion` (apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-contract.ts:54; affordance-read.ts:122-131 sets it from `record?.version ?? 0`), so no new read is needed - only a filter.
- The item id a seat holds is `workItemIdFor(step.kind, step.aggregateId)` (apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts:116, exported) - the same helper the wrapper uses; match on it, never on aggregateId alone.
- Query refusals today: `queryRefusal()` = `createRuntimeError({ code: "INPUT_INVALID" })` (mcp-dispatch-port.ts:131-133). The runtime error registry (packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-error-registry.ts) is a closed roster with pinned tests; the parent DoD names `WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN` for a nonexistent id. The architect decides at plan time: register WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN (contracts row + its pins + any digest mirror) if that stays within the file budget, else reuse the registry's existing not-found class code and RECORD the reading in planningNotes + a row comment; either way code AND layer are asserted.
- apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:178-195 pins that every served query kind refuses with something other than the generic INPUT_INVALID and that unserved kinds still get INPUT_INVALID - the kind roster does not change in this row (no new query kind).
- Test harness: apps/daemon/src/mcp-dispatch-port.test.ts builds `createMcpDispatchPort({ affordances, ... })` (:50, :129, :163) and calls `port.dispatchQueryBytes(...)` (:188+). Live report that motivates this: memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04 (60.1 KB dump for a nonexistent id; the harness truncates large MCP results so `claimAggregateVersion` is unreachable).

FEATURE: payload `{ workItemId }` -> `{ outcome: "SURFACE_ITEM", readAt, step }` where `step` is the ONE ChainStep whose workItemIdFor matches (claim + claimAggregateVersion included), well under 8 KB; a payload without `workItemId` keeps today's bytes exactly; `{ workItemId }` that matches no step -> the not-found refusal (code + layer); a non-string / empty workItemId -> INPUT_INVALID.
definitionOfDone: `work.get_context {workItemId}` over `dispatchQueryBytes` returns `{ outcome: "SURFACE_ITEM", readAt, step }` with `step.claimAggregateVersion` present and the encoded response under 8 KB for a surface of at least 20 steps (test builds one); the step is selected by `workItemIdFor(step.kind, step.aggregateId)` (test includes two steps sharing an aggregateId with different kinds and asserts the right one).

A nonexistent `workItemId` refuses with the chosen not-found code (WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN when registered, else the registry's existing not-found code named in planningNotes) - test asserts code AND layer; a non-string or empty `workItemId` refuses INPUT_INVALID (code asserted).

Payload-less call is byte-identical to today: a golden fixture of the response bytes for a fixed surface is pinned in mcp-dispatch-port.test.ts BEFORE the change (commit shows the fixture added first) and stays green after.

apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts pins unchanged (served/unserved query refusal arms green); if mcp-dispatch-port.ts would exceed 400 physical lines the handler is extracted to `mcp-work-context-query.ts` with its `.js` bridge and `wc -l` of both files quoted.

implementationPlan.description: NEW MODULE + ITS TEST (TDD: test first). Create apps/daemon/src/mcp-work-context-query.ts (<=250 physical lines) + bridge apps/daemon/src/mcp-work-context-query.js with exactly `export * from "./mcp-work-context-query.ts";`. Exports: `SURFACE_ITEM = "SURFACE_ITEM" as const`, `WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN = "WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN" as const`, `type SurfaceItem = Readonly<{ outcome: typeof SURFACE_ITEM; step: ChainStep; nextAllowedCommands: readonly NextAllowedCommand[]; planningGoalRef: string | null; planningAuthority: <the per-run entry type of planningAuthorityByRun> | null }>`, and `answerWorkContextQuery(payload: unknown, surface: AffordanceSurface | AffordanceRefused): SurfaceItem | AffordanceRefused | AffordanceSurface | { readonly code: "INPUT_INVALID" }` (a pure function, no bytes, no port). Rules, in this order: (1) surface not `outcome: "SURFACE"` -> return the refusal untouched (today's behaviour); (2) payload `undefined` OR a plain object WITHOUT own key `workItemId` -> return the whole surface object untouched (byte identity is the caller's job: it must serialise the SAME object reference); (3) payload not a plain object, or `workItemId` not a non-empty string -> `{ code: "INPUT_INVALID" }` (the port maps it to `queryRefusal()`); (4) find the unique step with `workItemIdFor(step.kind, step.aggregateId) === workItemId` (import from ./http/affordance-read.js:116 - never match on aggregateId alone); none -> `Object.freeze({ code: WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN, detail: `no step on the surface has workItemId ${workItemId}`, layer: AFFORDANCE_SURFACE_LAYER, outcome: "REFUSED" })` (exactly the AffordanceRefused shape, affordance-contract.ts:77-82, layer constant :18 - reuse, no new *_LAYER); found -> the SurfaceItem with `nextAllowedCommands` filtered to entries whose target-aggregate field equals the step's aggregateId (read NextAllowedCommand in affordance-contract.ts for the field name and cite it in a comment), `planningGoalRef = surface.planningGoalRefs[step.aggregateId] ?? null`, `planningAuthority = surface.planningAuthorityByRun[step.aggregateId] ?? null` (guard with Object.hasOwn - both maps are wire-shaped records), everything frozen. Test apps/daemon/src/mcp-work-context-query.test.ts: (a) refused surface passes through by reference; (b) payload undefined / {} return the same surface object (`toBe`); (c) INPUT_INVALID for payload null, array, string, `{workItemId: ""}`, `{workItemId: 7}`; (d) WORK_ITEM_UNKNOWN with layer 'AFFORDANCE_SURFACE' and the detail naming the id for a missing item; (e) the two steps sharing an aggregateId resolve to the right one by kind; (f) nextAllowedCommands filtered (one matching, one not), planning fields null when absent and present when keyed; (g) `Object.isFrozen` on the item and its arrays; (h) `JSON.stringify(item).length < 8192` for the 20-step surface. Run the new test file, count line quoted.
